title: Irrationality of finite logarithms in a congruence-class adèle ring
summary: Finite logarithms can be defined in the ``poor man's adèle ring" $\mathcal{A}$ using Fermat quotients modulo sufficiently large primes. This ring contains $\mathbb{Q}$ and outside the trivial cases, Matsusaka and Seki have shown that finite logarithms cannot take non-zero rational values in $\mathcal{A}$. Furthermore, a theorem of Silverman shows they are not zero, assuming the $abc$-conjecture.
